body:
USDC is a stablecoin pegged to the US dollar, and on the Solana network it moves in seconds and costs a fraction of a cent. That makes it one of the most convenient ways to pay an order at One Stop Vape Store: the amount you send is essentially your dollar total, so there is no exchange-rate movement to worry about, and USDC payments qualify for our 10% crypto discount. This guide explains what you need, walks through each step, covers the mistakes that cause most problems, explains how detection works and compares USDC on Solana with other options. It is for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## What you need
You need a wallet that supports Solana and holds USDC, such as a popular browser or mobile Solana wallet, or an exchange that allows USDC withdrawals on Solana. If you use a self-custody wallet, you also need a tiny amount of SOL in the same wallet to cover the network fee, because Solana fees are paid in SOL even when you send USDC. A few cents' worth is plenty. If you use an exchange, the exchange usually deducts the fee for you, often in USDC.

## Why USDC on Solana
- **Speed:** transfers usually finish in seconds.
- **Cost:** the fee is a fraction of a cent, so almost all of the 10% saving stays with you.
- **Stable amount:** because USDC tracks the dollar, you owe the same dollar value regardless of market moves.
- **Simple matching:** the amount is predictable, so detection is straightforward.

If you want a general explanation of why networks matter, read [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/).

## Step by step
1. Fill your cart, choose options such as strength and pack size on the product page and go to checkout. Enter your contact and shipping details and confirm you are 21 or older.
2. Choose Cryptocurrency at checkout, then USDC. Solana is the only network offered for USDC at our store.
3. In the payment window, copy the wallet address or scan the QR code. Use the copy button to avoid typing errors.
4. In your wallet, choose Send, select USDC and paste the address. Check the first and last characters.
5. Enter the amount shown and confirm.
6. Press "I have paid". Your order is placed and you land on the status page, where your payment is looked for on the Solana network and confirmed automatically.

## How detection works
Our system reads public Solana data for the shop wallet and looks for an incoming USDC transfer that fits your order: the right token, the right address, a dollar value close to your total, a recent time and a transaction that has not paid another order. When a transfer matches, we email you and the order moves into processing. Because USDC is a dollar stablecoin, the amount matches your total closely, which keeps tolerance concerns small. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/).

## Common mistakes
- **Sending USDC on a different network, such as Ethereum.** It will not arrive at our Solana address and may not be recoverable. Select Solana in your wallet or exchange.
- **Sending SOL instead of USDC.** They are different assets. If you chose USDC at checkout, send USDC.
- **Forgetting a little SOL for fees in a self-custody wallet.** Without it, the transfer cannot be made.
- **Sending a different stablecoin.** USDT is a different token with its own options. Choose it at checkout if you prefer USDT. See [USDT on ERC20 or TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/).
- **Resending a pending payment.** Check the status page and contact us first.

## Exchange withdrawals
If you pay from an exchange, choose USDC as the asset and Solana as the network on the withdrawal screen. Check the minimum and the fee, and if the exchange deducts its fee from the amount you enter, add the fee on top so the full amount arrives. Some exchanges hold new withdrawal addresses for a short security period. Our guide to [sending crypto from an exchange to a wallet](/blog/send-crypto-from-an-exchange-to-a-wallet/) covers the details.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is USDC the same as USDT?
No. Both are dollar stablecoins issued by different companies, and each exists on several networks. At our store, USDC is offered on Solana, and USDT is offered on Ethereum (ERC20) and Tron (TRC20). Choose the one your wallet holds.

### Do I get the 10% discount with USDC?
Yes. The discount is calculated on your product subtotal and applied automatically when you choose Cryptocurrency. Shipping is added afterward, and free shipping applies to orders of $200 or more after discount. See [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/).

### What if my wallet shows a different network name?
Look for Solana, SOL or SPL in the network list. If your wallet or exchange does not offer Solana for USDC, choose a different token or network that it does support.

### Can I buy USDC if I do not have any?
Yes. Read [how to buy crypto with a card](/blog/how-to-buy-crypto-with-a-card/). Buy USDC, choose Solana as the network when you withdraw, and then send it to our address.

## After your payment is confirmed
You receive an email, and your order status updates. We process orders within 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse and ship with tracking by USPS or UPS. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) and [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/).

## If your payment looks short
If the status page shows underpaid, do not resend the full amount. A small shortfall is usually caused by an exchange fee being deducted from the amount. Contact us with your order reference and transaction hash, and we will tell you what is needed. See [underpaid messages](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/). Browse the [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) range, and compare every option in [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What happens after you pay with USDC on Solana
USDC transfers on Solana are usually detected within seconds to a couple of minutes, and the status page updates on its own. Once your payment is confirmed, you receive an email and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and the carrier, USPS or UPS, delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). If you need to change something, read [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/) before your order ships.

## Staying protected when you pay with USDC
Only trust payment instructions that come through our official email, our WhatsApp number or your private order page. Check that your wallet or exchange is set to the Solana network and the USDC asset before you confirm, because USDC on another network will not reach our address. We never ask for your passwords, PINs, card numbers, private keys or recovery phrases, and no genuine order needs them. Be wary of anyone who contacts you out of the blue claiming to represent the store, offers a different address or account to pay or pushes you to pay quickly outside the order. If a message does not match your order number and amount exactly, stop and contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) before you send anything. For more on keeping your account details secure, see [gift card code security tips](/blog/gift-card-code-security-tips/) and [why we need your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/).

## A worked example
Suppose your cart is $320. Paying with USDC applies the 10% discount, so the product total is $288.00, and shipping is free because the amount after discount is above $200. The payment window shows 288 USDC. In a self-custody wallet holding USDC and a few cents of SOL, you choose Send, select USDC, paste the address, enter 288 and confirm. The fee is a fraction of a cent, paid in SOL. If you use an exchange that deducts a 1 USDC withdrawal fee from the amount, enter 289 so that 288 arrives. You press "I have paid", the status page detects the transfer and your order is confirmed. Because USDC tracks the dollar, there is no rate movement to worry about.

## Comparing USDC on Solana with the alternatives
- **USDT on Tron (TRC20):** also cheap and fast, widely supported by exchanges. See [USDT ERC20 vs TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/).
- **SOL:** the same network and speed, but the amount moves with the price. See [paying with Solana](/blog/pay-with-solana-sol/).
- **Bitcoin:** the most widely held, but slower to confirm. See [how to pay with Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/).

## A final checklist before you send
- Choose USDC and the Solana network in your wallet or exchange.
- Keep a few cents of SOL in a self-custody wallet for the fee.
- Add the exchange fee on top if it is deducted from the amount.
- Compare the address with the window before you confirm.

USDC on Solana is one of the simplest crypto routes because the amount is stable and fees are tiny. If anything looks wrong, contact us before you resend.

faq.a: Yes. All supported cryptocurrencies save 10% on your order total.

faq.a: It will not arrive at our Solana address and may not be recoverable. Contact us immediately with your order reference and transaction hash.
Yes. USDC tracks the US dollar, so you owe essentially your dollar total after the discount.

faq.a: Use a provider such as an exchange or card-purchase service, choose Solana as the network when you withdraw, and send it to the address in our window.
